cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: How Much Do You Know?
cards.instruction: Probe for what others know while revealing as little as possible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. When you say you heard about the party, which part?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake went over the balcony. Was that before you left?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Who gave you the timing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody. Your brother says there's a video.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Have you watched it, or are we both relying on my brother?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims teaching but never identifies what was taught; A3 nearly-doing-it praise is not tied to B2 timing question and A5 drops training.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 timing question leads to A3 source question; B4 video report feeds A5 watched-or-heard distinction.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants to establish A presence; B4 identifies a possible source rather than handing A a random cue.

heightening.evidence: A5 narrows the information channel but does not develop the claim to have trained B.

specificity.evidence: A1 party and B2 balcony cake supply an intelligible rumor exchange.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 nearly-doing-it is detachable commentary rather than a correction of B actual investigative practice.
